s0301.literal: As for having rivers and mountains within and without, gold and boiling water impregnable, clearing Long Shou to oppose the halls, cutting Mount Hua to serve as wall—mixed barbarians relied on it, strong troops at ease.
s0301.idiomatic: Within and without lay rivers and mountains, defenses firm as metal and boiling water; Long Shou was cleared to front the halls, Mount Hua hewn into a wall. Mixed barbarians leaned on it, and their armies stood secure.

s0302.literal: The Duke turned this earth's axle and resisted this heaven's net; in less than a morning he made none remain; military bearing was very solemn and state affairs were being repaired; things again valued the track of caps and robes, the people again gazed on rites and music; Chu people filled the roads, competing to trace Duke Ye; Han elders harbored grief, all rejoicing in the Intendant.
s0302.idiomatic: The Duke turned the earth's pivot and met heaven's net; before a full morning none were left; the host was grave and government was set right again; caps and robes returned to their proper order, and the people looked once more to rites and music. Chu folk thronged the roads to follow Duke Ye's path; Han elders who had mourned now rejoiced with the metropolitan intendant.

s0303.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0303.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0304.literal: When internal troubles first quieted and feudal lords went out through the passes, outer commanderies relayed beacon fires and the Xianbei violated the frontiers—all were Qiequ and Danghu, honored frontier kings; Ji horses ranged at Huainan and barbarian pipes stirred north of Xu.
s0304.idiomatic: When civil strife first stilled and the lords marched out of the passes, distant prefectures lit the beacons and Xianbei raided the frontier—Qiequ and Danghu, every honored king of the marches; horses of Ji swept Huainan, and barbarian pipes sounded north of Xu.

s0305.literal: The Duke's naval forces and infantry, crossing different wilds and spanning the river, annihilated the goats and pigs; none did not stop clinging to trees; chariots none left; meeting mud they turned; return horses all destroyed.
s0305.idiomatic: The Duke sent fleet and foot across strange country and the great river, wiped out the goat-and-pig foe, and left none clinging to trees for refuge; not a war chariot escaped; those who met the mire turned back, and every returning team was destroyed.

s0306.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0306.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0307.literal: The Duke overcame disasters and toiled for the imperial house, but Sun Ning's faction in turn opened barbarian hearts; between the Yi and Luo all became barbarian garrisons; though Jinling had fine aura and stone ramparts heaven-strict, morning was dark with barbarian dust and night clamorous with barbarian drums.
s0307.idiomatic: The Duke had quelled calamity and labored for the throne, yet Sun Ning's party stirred the barbarian heart anew; between the Yi and Luo every post was a barbarian camp. Though Jinling still breathed noble air and its stone ramparts were heaven-tall, by day barbarian dust dimmed the court and by night barbarian drums roared.

s0308.literal: The Duke had drawn the three stratagems and deployed the eight formations, and barely raised the spirit
s0308.idiomatic: The Duke had laid the three stratagems and spread the eight arrays, and barely raised the spirit

s0310.literal: Editorial footnote marker 0. Editorial footnote marker 30. banner; he also drew the golden mace; all ugly captives were taken; all returned to the high walls; unlike Li Guang, who executed all, like Pang Yuan, who pardoned all.
s0310.idiomatic: See editorial note 0. See editorial note 30. banner; he also drew the golden mace; every foul enemy was captured and sent back to the high walls—not like Li Guang, who slew all, but like Pang Yuan, who spared all.

s0311.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0311.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0312.literal: Ren Yue rebelled and changed sides, his fierce reputation unrepentant; Rong and Jie were greedy, wolf hearts unchanged; felt tents and wool pavilions pressed the northern gate to make camp; Wusun heavenly horses pointed at the eastern capital to form battle lines.
s0312.idiomatic: Ren Yue turned traitor and would not relent; Rong and Jie were ravenous, their wolf hearts unchanged; felt tents and wool pavilions camped against the northern gate; Wusun steeds of heaven massed toward the eastern capital in battle array.

s0313.literal: The Duke with left horn and right wing, winnow-sieve spread and wings extended, swept away the comet-star foe and drove off the Xianyun; the race of Long Di was buried at the state gate, chieftains with topknots were boiled in the army market; cast into Qin's pit all boiled, choking
s0313.idiomatic: The Duke with left horn and right wing, winnow-sieve spread and wings extended, swept the comet-star foe and drove the Xianyun; the race of Long Di was buried at the state gate, chieftains with topknots were boiled in the army market; cast into Qin's pit until all seethed, choking

s0315.literal: the Sui River so it did not flow.
s0315.idiomatic: the Sui River until it would not flow.

s0316.literal: Editorial footnote marker 31. This again is the Duke's merit.
s0316.idiomatic: See editorial note 31. This again is the Duke's merit.

s0317.literal: One minister held the center and himself broke the ritual vessels; a petty guardian of the Five Lakes vainly harbored the same evil.
s0317.idiomatic: One minister held the center and himself broke the ritual vessels; a petty guardian of the Five Lakes vainly shared the same treason.

s0318.literal: The Duke at dawn drove by double stages, girded robes and took up staff and halberd; the jade axe was about to be swung and the golden gong already warned; demon chieftains were shaken in terror and hastily begged for ashes and nails; he burned the coffin to show his magnanimity and burned books to settle their wavering hearts.
s0318.idiomatic: The Duke rode at dawn by forced stages, girded his robes, and took up staff and halberd; the jade axe was ready to fall and the golden gong already sounded; demon chieftains trembled and at once begged for ashes and nails; he burned the coffin to show his breadth and burned their writings to quiet their restless hearts.

s0319.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0319.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0320.literal: The bandit niche was fierce and overbearing, bullying and tyrannizing the Great Lake region, relying on arms and cruel endurance, trusting in calamity and clinging to disorder; from antiquity in lands of insect speech and bird tracks, chaos and vast flood—for any who were devoutly slaughtered, none was so cruel as this.
s0320.idiomatic: The rebel stronghold was brutal, ravaging the Great Lake country, trusting in arms and cruelty, leaning on disaster and chaos. Since antiquity, in lands of strange tongues and untouched wilds, no slaughter had matched this cruelty.

s0321.literal: Though the Duke's clan dwelt in Ru and Ying and his family sojourned in the southeast—the land where sages were bred and worthies born, the place where hidden virtue rose outstanding—he cherished his native soil and public and private alike burned with indignation; with outstanding heroic bearing, Editorial footnote marker 32. he took counsel and offered stratagem, slaughtered this great villain as if cooking a small fish.
s0321.idiomatic: Though his clan lay in Ru and Ying and his house sojourned in the southeast—the country that bred sages and bore worthies, where hidden virtue rose in splendor—he turned to his native soil and public and private wrath alike ran hot; in heroic stature, See editorial note 32. he took counsel and offered stratagem and slew that great villain as easily as cooking a small fish.

s0322.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0322.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0323.literal: Disorder and separation were long; bandits and robbers very many; on the left of Zhe the vicious chieftains linked arms in rebellion—was it only the Thousand Soldiers, Five Colonels, White Sparrow, and Yellow Dragon?
s0323.idiomatic: Years of chaos had piled up; bandits swarmed; on the Zhe left vicious chiefs joined in arms—far more than the Thousand Soldiers, Five Colonels, White Sparrow, and Yellow Dragon alone.

s0324.literal: Because the central army had no leader, the Duke chose close and worthy men; the traitor band reached its end and melted like ice; at the place where punishment was made Tang, Wen Ming moved his great awesomeness; between the Thunder Gate, Goujian carried out stern execution—heroic design and sage traces, different ages, same wind.
s0324.idiomatic: When the central army lacked a leader, the Duke chose kin and worthies; the traitors were driven to their end and melted like ice. Where punishments once made Tang, he moved heaven's dread; at the Thunder Gate, Goujian's stern justice lived again—heroic rule and sage footprints, another age, the same wind.

s0325.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0325.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0326.literal: A kinsman of Youhu was stubborn and fierce, not a guest; relying on clan alliance he plotted peril for the altars; he displayed troops at Huize and his momentum shook the capital; driving southern barbarians, he already styled himself eastern emperor.
s0326.idiomatic: A kinsman of Youhu was stubborn and would not submit; leaning on clan ties he threatened the state; he paraded troops at Huize and his power shook the capital; leading southern tribes, he already called himself emperor of the east.

s0327.literal: The Duke discussed warfare in the hall of the temple and decided victory between the chopping block and meat-stand; Kou, Jia, Fan, and Teng floated down the river through the rapids; in one morning they were leveled—no need to wait for the field army; ten thousand li were clarified, not labor for the Pacifier of the West.
s0327.idiomatic: The Duke debated war in the ancestral hall and won between the block and the stand; Kou, Jia, Fan, and Teng swept downriver through the rapids; in one morning they were struck down without waiting for the main host; ten thousand li grew clear, no toil for Ma Yuan's heir.

s0328.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0328.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0329.literal: The demon band of Yuzhang relied on mountains and marshes, repaired armor and gathered strength, through many years; Editorial footnote marker 33. they joined in horizontal alliances as far as Jiao and Guang.
s0329.idiomatic: The demon host of Yuzhang held the hills and swamps, repaired armor and hoarded strength for years; See editorial note 33. they knit alliances from province to province, even to Jiao and Guang.

s0330.literal: Lü Jia was already taken; Wu Pi was already
s0330.idiomatic: Lü Jia was already taken; Wu Pi was already

s0332.literal: broken; Editorial footnote marker 34. he ordered me to return the army and punish their disobedience; linked camps were all uprooted, the false party was seized; he displayed sage martial at Kuang Mountain and turned the spirit banner at the Li outlet.
s0332.idiomatic: broken; See editorial note 34. he ordered our withdrawal to chastise their disobedience; camp after camp was torn up and the false faction captured; he showed sage martial on Kuang Mountain and turned the spirit banner at the Li outlet.

s0333.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0333.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0334.literal: From the eight cords and nine wilds, like melons split and beans scattered, men stole imperial titles and kingship, linking prefectures and comparing counties.
s0334.idiomatic: From the eight directions and nine realms, realm after realm split like melons and beans; men stole thrones and crowns, linking prefecture to prefecture and county to county.

s0335.literal: The Duke's martial spirit was already fulfilled and civil virtue again proclaimed; with folded letters and galloping dispatches his wind and teaching reached far; as far as the blue sky bathing the sun and deep stillness without thunder, north to the land of true men and south beyond the land of women—all none but bent the knee in worship, seeking officials and knocking at the gate.
s0335.idiomatic: The Duke's martial power was full and his civil teaching spread again; letters flew and his influence ran far—to the blue sky that bathes the sun, to the deep hush without thunder; north to the country of true men and south past the land of women—none but knelt in homage and begged for officers at his gate.

s0336.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0336.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0337.literal: The capital suffered calamity and disorder, cold and warmth heaped up in turn; the twin towers rose and fell, the nine gates stood empty and wide.
s0337.idiomatic: The capital had known calamity upon calamity, season piled on season; the twin towers swayed, the nine gates gaped empty.

s0338.literal: Could one still look back on the Qin palace?
s0338.idiomatic: Could one still look back on the Qin palace?

s0339.literal: Could the Lu hall still remain?
s0339.idiomatic: Could the Lu hall still stand?

s0340.literal: The five capitals' capped officials and the hundred ministers and grandees—barbarian dress and loose sashes all became barbarian custom; high caps and thick shoes scarcely returned to Chinese style; the song of Prince Weizi of Song on wheat ears, the sigh of the Zhou grandee on millet fallen—compared with this, they were not enough to be called grief.
s0340.idiomatic: Officials of the five capitals and the hundred ministers and grandees wore barbarian dress and loose sashes until all was barbarian custom; high caps and thick shoes barely recalled Chinese ways. Prince Weizi's song on standing grain, the Zhou minister's lament on millet—set beside this, they were hardly grief at all.

s0341.literal: The Duke sought his robes before dawn, ate after the sun slanted and worked until late morning; he raised and built the palace quarters, a sight for far and near; suburban schools and ancestral altars' rites, the six tallies and ten ranks' regulations—again one heard the style of Grand Beginning and again trod the legacy of Eternal Peace.
s0341.idiomatic: The Duke rose before dawn for his robes, ate after the sun slanted and labored until late morning; he rebuilt the palace quarters, a sight for far and near; suburban schools and ancestral rites, the six tallies and ten ranks—once more the air of Grand Beginning returned, and the tracks of Eternal Peace were laid again.

s0342.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0342.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0343.literal: The Duke had merit that saved the world, further weighted with bright virtue; he concentrated spirit and embodied the Way, united virtue and matched heaven; he took the hundred surnames as his heart and followed the myriad affairs to accomplish his task; he was ashamed if one thing were not a people of Tang and Yu, returning all who bear spirit to the realm of benevolence and longevity; highest virtue without claiming virtue, acting through non-action; summer long, spring born, showing benevolence and hiding use; loyalty and trust were treasure, wind and rain did not go astray; benevolence and grace were the foundation, cattle and sheep were not trampled; merit accomplished and rule settled, music played Xian and Cloud; securing the heights and governing the people, rites combined pattern and substance; he sought men in hill gardens and in lane skirts; the court had many gentlemen, the wilds no lost worthies; grain was rich as water and fire, merchants and craftsmen wealthy as the house of Xi Dun.
s0343.idiomatic: The Duke had saved the world and was crowned with bright virtue; he gathered his spirit in the Way and matched heaven in virtue; he made the people's heart his own and bent every affair to that end; he would be shamed if one soul were not a subject of Tang and Yu, and he brought all living beings into the realm of kindness and long life. Highest virtue did not boast virtue; he ruled through non-action; summer lengthened and spring gave birth; he showed benevolence and hid his power; loyalty and trust were his treasure, and wind and rain did not miss their season; kindness was his ground, and cattle and sheep went unharmed; when merit was done and order fixed, the music of Xian and Cloud was played; he secured the throne and governed the people, rites blending form and substance; he sought talent in hills and lanes; the court brimmed with gentlemen, the wilds held no hidden worth; grain lay rich as water and fire, and merchants and craftsmen prospered like the house of Xi Dun.

s0344.literal: Therefore heaven had no hidden treasure and earth showed auspicious signs; heavy dew and minister clouds clustered at dawn's glow; mountain carts and marsh horses, harnessed and at ease; already bright in the books, now flourishing in the historical records.
s0344.idiomatic: So heaven hid no treasure and earth offered omens; heavy dew and ministerial clouds gathered at dawn; mountain carts and marsh horses stood harnessed and at ease; glory already shone in the classics and now flourished in the annals.

s0345.literal: High merit surpassed the star-ordinances; accumulated virtue crowned Song and Hua—truly one of whom it could be said there was no claiming virtue.
s0345.idiomatic: His lofty merit outran the stars; his heaped virtue topped Song and Hua—truly a man of whom none could say he claimed virtue.

s0346.literal: I have also heard that former kings ruled the age, richly rewarded and honored the worthy, formally planted feudal chiefs, and gathered in punitive lords; the Two Souths were exalted beyond reach, the four borders far and wide; vast was the sea's surface, fief soil was Qi; lofty was Mount Tai, made marquis of Lu;
s0346.idiomatic: I have also heard that kings of old ruled the world, richly rewarded the worthy, set up feudal chiefs, and gathered punitive lords; the Two Souths stood beyond compare, the four borders stretched vast; the sea's edge was Qi; Mount Tai was high, and Lu was enfeoffed;

s0347.literal: and again there were those who aided the king against Zheng and flanked the move of Zhou; the Duke of Shao's command was thereby exalted, the rites of Heyang all complete;
s0347.idiomatic: and again those who aided the king against Zheng and steadied Zhou in its move; the Duke of Shao's commission was raised on high, the rites of Heyang all complete;

s0348.literal: how much more when one orders the cosmos—not only the merit of cutting off the turtle's legs, and broadly saves the black-haired people—not only the peril of boring through Dragon Gate.
s0348.idiomatic: how much more when one orders the cosmos—not only the feat of cutting the turtle's legs, and broadly saves the people—not only the hazard of boring Dragon Gate.

s0349.literal: Yet reward for merit and return for virtue were silent and unheard—this is why I sit with folded hands upon the throne and carry a full heart of unease.
s0349.idiomatic: Yet merit went unrewarded and virtue unreturned—that is why I sit with folded hands on the throne and bear this unease in my breast.

s0350.literal: Now I appoint you Chancellor of State, with the ten commanderies of Chenliu, South Danyang, and Xuancheng in South Yuzhou; Wuxing, Dongyang, Xin'an, and Xinning in Yangzhou; Yixing in South Xuzhou; and Poyang and Linchuan in Jiangzhou—and enfeoff you as Duke of Chen.
s0350.idiomatic: Now I make you chancellor of state, granting the ten commanderies of Chenliu, South Danyang, and Xuancheng in South Yuzhou; Wuxing, Dongyang, Xin'an, and Xinning in Yangzhou; Yixing in South Xuzhou; and Poyang and Linchuan in Jiangzhou—and enfeoff you as Duke of Chen.

s0351.literal: I bestow this azure earth and wrap it with white thatch, thereby fixing your state and establishing your altar of soil and grain.
s0351.idiomatic: I grant this azure earth wrapped in white thatch, fixing your state and founding your altar of soil and grain.

s0352.literal: In former times the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao divided Shaan, both serving as guardian teachers; Jin and Zheng among the feudal lords all served as ministers—combining inner and outer, the rite was truly fitting.
s0352.idiomatic: Of old the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao divided Shaan, both guardians; Jin and Zheng among the lords served as ministers—inner and outer together, as ritual required.

s0353.literal: Now I order the commissioner with staff, concurrent Grand Commandant Wang Tong, to present the chancellor's seal and sash and the Duke of Chen's seal and ribbon.
s0353.idiomatic: Now I order the commissioner with staff, concurrent grand commandant Wang Tong, to present the chancellor's seal and sash and the Duke of Chen's seal and ribbon.

s0354.literal: The commissioner with staff, concurrent Minister of Works Wang Chang, is to present the Duke of Chen's fief soil, gold beast tallies first through fifth on the left, Editorial footnote marker 35. bamboo envoy tallies first through tenth on the left.
s0354.idiomatic: The commissioner with staff, concurrent minister of works Wang Chang, is to present the Duke of Chen's fief soil, gold beast tallies one through five on the left, See editorial note 35. bamboo envoy tallies one through ten on the left.

s0355.literal: Editorial footnote marker 36. The chancellor's rank surpasses the three handles; his charge sums the hundred offices; his station is apart from the court ranks; ritual follows the matter and changes.
s0355.idiomatic: See editorial note 36. The chancellor's rank surpasses the three handles; he sums the hundred offices; his place stands apart from the court ranks; ritual follows the office and changes.

s0356.literal: Let him as chancellor sum the hundred affairs, remove the title Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and retain the previously lent staff of the palace attendant with cicada insignia, seals of the Supervisor of the Secretariat, seals of the Grand Tutor commanding inner and outer affairs, and the seal and patent of Duke of Yixing; his posts as Supreme Commander Who Pacifies, governor of Yangzhou, remain as before.
s0356.idiomatic: Let him as chancellor direct the hundred affairs, drop the title recorder of the Masters of Writing, and keep the previously lent palace attendant's staff with cicada insignia, the supervisor of the secretariat's seals, the grand tutor's seals for inner and outer command, and the seal and patent of Duke of Yixing; his posts as supreme commander who pacifies and governor of Yangzhou remain as before.

s0357.literal: I further add to the Duke the Nine Bestowals—respectfully hear the following commands: Because the Duke's rites are the state's pillar and beam, laws and measures hold the bit and bridle, the four bonds are all raised and the eight handles have pattern—therefore I bestow great carriage and war carriage, one each, and dark stallions, two teams of four.
s0357.idiomatic: I further grant the Duke the Nine Bestowals—hear the commands: Because your rites are the state's pillar and beam, laws and measures hold the reins, the four bonds stand firm and the eight handles have order—therefore I grant a great carriage and a war carriage, one each, and dark stallions, two teams of four.

s0358.literal: Because the Duke esteems grain and cheapens treasure, spreads ranks and awaits farmers, granaries are rich as the capital mound and the people know honor and shame—therefore I bestow the three-tier cap and robes, with red shoes besides.
s0358.idiomatic: Because you honor grain and cheapen jewels, spread ranks and wait on farmers, granaries brim like the capital mound and the people know shame and honor—therefore I grant the three-tier cap and robes, with red shoes besides.

s0359.literal: Because the Duke harmonizes yin and yang and admonishes in accord with the Odes, the three spirits truly descend and the myriad states are together in harmony—therefore I bestow suspended music and the six rows of dancers.
s0359.idiomatic: Because you harmonize yin and yang and counsel in the spirit of the Odes, the three spirits descend and the myriad states are at peace—therefore I grant suspended music and the dance of six rows.

s0360.literal: Because the Duke proclaims and guides the king's plans, broadly opens wind and teaching, wherever light and radiance reach leather and elephant must communicate—therefore I bestow vermilion doors to dwell in.
s0360.idiomatic: Because you proclaim the king's design and spread teaching abroad, wherever light falls even leather and ivory must reach you—therefore I grant vermilion doors to dwell in.

s0361.literal: Because the Duke raises the clear and lowers the turbid, reports virtue and advances the worthy, eminent scholars fill the court and recluses fill empty valleys—therefore I bestow the inner steps to ascend.
s0361.idiomatic: Because you raise the clear and lower the turbid, report virtue and advance the worthy, eminent scholars fill the court and recluses fill empty hills—therefore I grant the inner steps to ascend.

s0362.literal: Because the Duke stands lofty in the hall and temple as the age's model, checks enemies on the four borders and faces the eight wilds—therefore I bestow three hundred martial guard warriors.
s0362.idiomatic: Because you stand lofty in hall and temple as the age's model, check foes on the four borders and face the eight wilds—therefore I grant three hundred martial guard warriors.

s0363.literal: Editorial footnote marker 37. Because the Duke holds this bright punishment, aiming at punishments set aside, none who seem respectful is spared, none who violates discipline escapes—therefore I bestow axe and yue, one each.
s0363.idiomatic: See editorial note 37. Because you hold this bright punishment, aiming at the day when punishments fall still, none who seem respectful is spared, none who breaks law escapes—therefore I grant axe and yue, one each.

s0364.literal: Because the Duke's heroic plan and far measure cross and tread Mount Song and the eastern sea, wrap one cart of documents and bundle the whole realm—therefore I bestow one red bow, one hundred red arrows, ten black bows, and one thousand black arrows.
s0364.idiomatic: Because your heroic design and far sight cross Mount Song and the eastern sea, wrap one cart of writs and hold the whole realm in your hand—therefore I grant one red bow, one hundred red arrows, ten black bows, and one thousand black arrows.

s0365.literal: Because the Duke's heaven's warp and earth's woof penetrate dark and bright, spring dew and autumn frost, truly reverent in grain offerings—therefore I bestow one jar of black millet ale, with jade libation cup besides.
s0365.idiomatic: Because your heaven's warp and earth's woof run through dark and bright, spring dew and autumn frost, truly reverent at the grain altar—therefore I grant one jar of black millet ale, with jade libation cup besides.

s0366.literal: In the state of Chen, from chancellor down, all follow the old forms.
s0366.idiomatic: In the state of Chen, from chancellor down, all follow the old forms.

s0368.literal: Respectfully follow my command, assist the august heaven, broadly build the state and clan, truly raise the great enterprise, to glorify my Founder's fair mandate!
s0368.idiomatic: Respectfully follow my command, assist august heaven, broadly build the state and clan, truly raise the great enterprise, and glorify my Founder's fair mandate!

s0369.literal: On wuchen day in the tenth month the Founder's rank was advanced to king, with the twenty commanderies of Kuaiji, Linhai, Yongjia, and Jian'an in Yangzhou; Jinling and Xinyi in South Xuzhou; and Xunyang, Yuzhang, Ancheng, and Luling in Jiangzhou added as before to enlarge the state of Chen.
s0369.idiomatic: On wuchen day in the tenth month the Founder's rank was raised to king, adding twenty commanderies—Kuaiji, Linhai, Yongjia, and Jian'an in Yangzhou; Jinling and Xinyi in South Xuzhou; and Xunyang, Yuzhang, Ancheng, and Luling in Jiangzhou—to enlarge the state of Chen.

s0370.literal: His posts as chancellor, governor of Yangzhou, and Supreme Commander Who Pacifies remained as before.
s0370.idiomatic: His posts as chancellor, governor of Yangzhou, and supreme commander who pacifies remained as before.

s0371.literal: He was further ordered as King of Chen to wear twelve tassels on the cap, raise the Son of Heaven's banners, clear the road when going out and on returning, ride the golden-root carriage, drive six horses, have five-season secondary carriages prepared, set yak-tail and cloud banners, music and dance of eight rows, and establish bell frames and palace suspended instruments.
s0371.idiomatic: He was further ordered as king of Chen to wear twelve cap tassels, raise the Son of Heaven's banners, clear the road on exit and return, ride the golden-root carriage drawn by six horses, keep five-season secondary carriages, set yak-tail and cloud banners, music and dance of eight rows, and establish bell frames and palace instruments.

s0372.literal: The titles for the king's consort, princes, and princesses, and the hundred offices of the Chen administration—all followed the old statutes.
s0372.idiomatic: Titles for the king's consort, princes, and princesses, and the hundred offices of the Chen administration—all followed the old statutes.

s0373.literal: On xinwei day the Liang emperor abdicated the throne to Chen; an edict said:
s0373.idiomatic: On xinwei day the Liang emperor abdicated to Chen; the edict said:

s0374.literal: The five movements begin anew, the three orthodoxies succeed one another; to shepherd the black-haired people belongs to the sage and worthy, whereby one can weave heaven and earth, cover the four quarters, greatly shelter the people, and spread the grand achievement.
s0374.idiomatic: The five phases turn anew, the three calendars succeed one another; to shepherd the people belongs to the sage, who can weave heaven and earth, cover the realm, shelter the masses, and spread the grand achievement.

s0375.literal: Changing darkness to brightness, age piled upon age on the same track—hundred kings followed in martial steps, all by this rule.
s0375.idiomatic: Darkness gave way to light, age after age on one track—hundred kings followed in martial steps, all by this rule.

s0376.literal: Liang virtue sank and faded; calamity and disorder arose in succession; at the beginning of Great Clarity one was trapped by the long serpent; in the season of Receiving Sagacity one again suffered the ravenous boar.
s0376.idiomatic: Liang virtue sank and faded; calamity and disorder arose in succession; at the beginning of Great Clarity one was trapped by the long serpent; in the season of Receiving Sagacity one again suffered the ravenous boar.

s0377.literal: When it reached Heavenly Completion, the sacred vessel was again stolen; the three luminaries swiftly sank, the seven temples lacked sacrifice; living beings were already extinguished, the bronze mandate fell—my martial and primal fortune was like a dangling tassel; quietly I pondered difficulty and stripping, evening vigilance filled my breast.
s0377.idiomatic: When it reached Heavenly Completion the sacred vessel was stolen again; the three lights swiftly dimmed, the seven temples went without sacrifice; living beings were spent, the bronze mandate fell—my martial and primal fortune hung like a dangling tassel; quietly I pondered ruin and stripping, and evening vigilance filled my breast.

s0378.literal: The Chancellor of State, King of Chen, had mandate from heaven and descending spirit from the peak; heaven and earth united in virtue, the sun-staff and stars alike bright; he saved the altars from the crosscurrent, lifted the hundred million from charcoal; east he punished rebellion, north he destroyed the Xianyun fiends; awesomeness reached the four seas, benevolence spread to the myriad states; he restored collapsed music, again raised extinct rites; Confucian halls were repaired, barbarian posts stood empty of scouts; great merit lay in Shun, splendid achievement only in Yu—vast, vast, none could name it.
s0378.idiomatic: The chancellor of state, king of Chen, had mandate from heaven and spirit from the sacred peak; heaven and earth shared his virtue, sun and stars burned bright with him; he saved the altars from the flood, lifted the millions from the coals; east he punished rebels, north he destroyed the Xianyun; his awesomeness filled the four seas, his kindness spread to every state; he restored fallen music and raised extinct rites; Confucian halls were repaired, barbarian posts stood empty; his merit matched Shun, his achievement only Yu—vast beyond naming.

s0379.literal: White rings came as tribute—was it only in the age of august Yu? White pheasants entered tribute—not only on the exalted Zhou day.
s0379.idiomatic: White rings came as tribute—was that only in the age of august Yu? White pheasants were offered—not only in exalted Zhou.

s0380.literal: Thus treasures were offered on rivers and land, omens shown in mist and cloud; sweet dew and sweet springs morning and evening welled and surged; fine grain and red grass sprouted thick in the suburbs.
s0380.idiomatic: Treasures rose from rivers and land, omens from mist and cloud; sweet dew and sweet springs welled morning and evening; fine grain and red grass sprouted thick in the suburbs.

s0381.literal: The Way was clear in distant ages, merit reached the august vault; bright, bright was high heaven, glory to sun and moon; change of the old was written in the dark signs, succession of virtue shown in the charts; lawsuits had their return, songs of praise turned this way—the heavenly succession truly had its place.
s0381.idiomatic: The Way shone in distant ages, merit reached heaven; bright was high heaven, glory to sun and moon; change of the old was written in the dark signs, succession of virtue in the charts; lawsuits found their judge, songs of praise turned here—the heavenly succession truly had its lord.

s0382.literal: Though I am mediocre and small, dark on antiquity, long have I traced exaltation and replacement; how dare I forget the former dynasties' handed statutes and the utmost wish of men and spirits?
s0382.idiomatic: Though I am mediocre and small, dark on antiquity, long have I traced rise and fall; how dare I forget the former dynasties' statutes and the utmost wish of men and spirits?

s0383.literal: Now I yield the throne to a separate palace and respectfully abdicate to Chen, all following the stories of Tang and Yu, Song and Qi.
s0383.idiomatic: Now I yield the throne to a separate palace and respectfully abdicate to Chen, following the stories of Tang and Yu, Song and Qi.

s0385.literal: I address you, King of Chen: in high antiquity when living beings first arose, before Lilian and Lilu, in the age of Rongcheng and Great Court—when knotted cords and bird script, deep darkness and vast confusion—therefore none can detail it.
s0385.idiomatic: I address you, king of Chen: in high antiquity when life first arose, before Lilian and Lilu, in the age of Rongcheng and Great Court—knotted cords and bird script, deep darkness and vast confusion—none can tell it in full.

s0386.literal: From the rulers Fuxi, Shennong, Xuanyuan, and Haohao to the masters Yaotang and Youyu—some draped robes and ruled the four seas, some through non-action made the myriad surnames their children; to hold it was like driving a rotten rope, to leave it like slipping off worn shoes.
s0386.idiomatic: From Fuxi, Shennong, Xuanyuan, and Haohao to Yaotang and Youyu—some ruled the four seas with draped robes, some through non-action made the people their children; to hold the throne was like driving rotten rope, to leave it like slipping off worn shoes.

s0387.literal: Barely meeting Xu You, one could then yield the throne; briefly encountering Shan Juan, one at once made him king.
s0387.idiomatic: Meet Xu You, and one could yield the throne; meet Shan Juan, and one at once made him king.

s0388.literal: Thus one knows the dark terrace and jade armillary have nothing to do with honor; golden-root carriage and jade chariot show the sign of ruling.
s0388.idiomatic: So the dark terrace and jade armillary have nothing to do with rank; golden-root carriage and jade chariot show the sign of sovereignty.

s0389.literal: When south he viewed the river islet and east he sank the carved jade, essence was exhausted and aged diligence already weary—then he raised his head and laughed, giving only to the worthy; suddenly he made a song, choosing ability and then conferring; surviving wind and remaining heat are clear in the books.
s0389.idiomatic: When south he viewed the river islet and east he sank the carved jade, his essence was spent and aged toil weary—then he raised his head and laughed, giving only to the worthy; suddenly he sang, chose the able, and conferred; that surviving wind shines clear in the books.

s0390.literal: Han and Wei followed in succession—this is the old reality.
s0390.idiomatic: Han and Wei followed in succession—this is the old reality.

s0391.literal: Song and Qi in receiving and giving again enlarged this principle.
s0391.idiomatic: Song and Qi in receiving and giving again enlarged this principle.

s0392.literal: Our Founder met the season and stroked the mandate, grasped the pivot and ruled the realm; the three queens again shone, ancestors together sage.
s0392.idiomatic: Our Founder met the season and took the mandate, grasped the pivot and ruled the realm; the three queens shone again, ancestors together sage.

s0393.literal: When the time reached the yang nine, the ravenous boar repeatedly devoured, the western capital lost control, barbarians and Di invaded one another; then one usurped Heavenly Completion and lightly toyed with the bronze tripod; trembling were the black-haired people, as if corners collapsing; dim, dim the august pole, Editorial footnote marker 38. about to be more than a dangling tassel.
s0393.idiomatic: When the time reached the yang nine, the ravenous boar devoured again, the western capital lost its helm, barbarians and Di invaded in turn; then one usurped Heavenly Completion and lightly toyed with the bronze tripod; the people trembled as if their corners would break; dim was the august pole, See editorial note 38. about to hang like a dangling tassel.

s0394.literal: You alone are sage and divine, reverent, bright, cultured, and thoughtful; the two principles moved in concert, the four seasons in proper order; heaven bestowed wisdom and courage, men raised the heroic and outstanding; pearl forehead and sun corner, dragon stride and martial step, Editorial footnote marker 39. at first you flung up your sleeves, at the mao hour you aided the king; lightning swept Panyu, clouds cleared Pengli, leveled the chief villain, settled our capital region.
s0394.idiomatic: You alone are sage and divine, reverent, bright, cultured, and thoughtful; the two principles moved as one, the four seasons in order; heaven gave wisdom and courage, men raised the hero; pearl brow and sun corner, dragon stride and martial step, See editorial note 39. at first you flung up your sleeves, at the mao hour you aided the king; lightning swept Panyu, clouds cleared Pengli, cut down the chief villain, settled our capital.

s0395.literal: When you received the king's felicitation and the emperor's enlargement, you traded this cap and shoes; already acting as Yi and Huo, you thereby protected the young ruler.
s0395.idiomatic: When you received the king's blessing and the emperor's trust, you took this cap and shoes; already acting as Yi and Huo, you protected the young ruler.

s0396.literal: Zhenze and Kuaiji all harbored rebellion; Xianyun and Jie, ugly barbarians, thrice disturbed the imperial capital; barely ordering a partial army, the two regions destroyed themselves; a light campaign against the Xianyun, the six Rong all exterminated.
s0396.idiomatic: Zhenze and Kuaiji all harbored rebellion; Xianyun and Jie, foul barbarians, thrice disturbed the capital; with a partial host alone the two regions destroyed themselves; a light strike at the Xianyun, the six Rong all wiped out.

s0397.literal: Lingnan rebelled and scattered, Xiang and Ying joined in alliance; the bandit chief was already taken, the vicious chieftain's head sent; Editorial footnote marker 40. thereby the hundred offices were timely in order, the four gates truly harmonious; none thought but submitted, none far but reached; above it reached the vaulted sky, below it leaked the deep springs; Editorial footnote marker 41. dragons and fish all appeared, songs of praise turned to you.
s0397.idiomatic: Lingnan rebelled and scattered, Xiang and Ying joined in league; the bandit chief was taken, the vicious chieftain's head delivered; See editorial note 40. the hundred offices kept their seasons, the four gates stood in harmony; none but submitted, none so far they did not come; above it reached heaven, below the deep springs; See editorial note 41. dragons and fish all appeared, songs of praise turned to you.

s0398.literal: How much more when the long comet lay across heaven—already a sign of spreading the new; the jade sun already eclipsed—truly a token of changing the surname.
s0398.idiomatic: How much more when the long comet crossed heaven—already a sign of the new order; the jade sun eclipsed—truly a token of changing the surname.

s0399.literal: Therefore at first founding the righteous army, purple clouds shone in splendor; at first honoring the lord, the yellow dragon bore the boat.
s0399.idiomatic: Therefore at first founding the righteous army, purple clouds shone; at first honoring the lord, the yellow dragon bore the boat.

s0400.literal: With blunt arrows and white pheasant tail-feathers, they climbed mountains to arrive; with white rings and jade disks, they came admiring virtue.
s0400.idiomatic: With blunt arrows and white pheasant feathers they climbed mountains to come; with white rings and jade disks they arrived admiring virtue.
